label: Start of copy phase in long sequences (first 2-3 recall steps, L>=8)
explanation: Fires almost only at the start of the copy phase: the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0, 40% of mass), the step that outputs original token 1 (43%), and less at recall_idx 2 (13%). Nearly silent during the original phase (3% of mass, mostly t=7-8 of L=9) and in the later copy phase. Firing rate and mass rise steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 58% of mass, L=8 25%, L<=6 under 6%), so it effectively tracks many outputs still to go (to_go 7-8). Within these positions it is strongly token-modulated and fires on only a minority of them (precision about 0.1): it prefers some tokens being output (z, l, k, 3, h, o, r, e, 2) and, at recall_idx 1, some fed-back first tokens (n, g, u). The highest activations are at recall_idx 1 with in_tok = first original token, e.g. n. I could not find a clean token rule, so precision is still low.
